questions.questionText:
Statement: Should registration of all pet dogs be made compulsory?
Arguments:
I. Yes, because dogs have four legs.
II. No, because some people keep cats.
Which of the following is a strong argument?
options: Only I is strong
Only II is strong
Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: A strong argument is relevant, specific and important to the question; vague, trivial, irrelevant or purely personal reasons are weak. Neither reason has any bearing on registration. Both are weak.
questions.shortcut: Ask: does the reason bear directly on the question with real consequences? Reject trivial, vague or irrelevant reasons.

questions.questionText:
Statement: Should national highways have more rest areas?
Arguments:
I. No, highways are meant for moving vehicles.
II. Yes, driver fatigue is a major cause of highway accidents and rest areas let drivers rest.
Which of the following is a strong argument?
options: Only I is strong
Only II is strong
Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: A strong argument is relevant, specific and important to the question; vague, trivial, irrelevant or purely personal reasons are weak. II links rest areas to safety. I is a vague statement of purpose.
questions.shortcut: Ask: does the reason bear directly on the question with real consequences? Reject trivial, vague or irrelevant reasons.
